templates_considered: AUTH-002 admin_endpoints_check_role: fits the role-check half; used as the starting point. Template scopes by tag 'admin' and its example function is require_admin; the workspace has neither, so I scoped by api_groups ['admin'] and used check_admin_role.
AUTH-020 own_records_only: does not fit; it is owner-by-user_id, and the ask is org_id tenancy for staff.
AUTH-030 no_self_promotion: related to /admin role safety but not asked for; not used.
AUTH-010 endpoints_need_login: not asked for; admin endpoints already use auth = 'users'.
CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login / DATA-010 no_pii_in_responses: not asked for; not used.
No template covers 'tenants reads filter by org_id'; key TEN-010 chosen (no template uses the TEN prefix).

rules.covers: Every endpoint under /admin (admin API group) checks the caller's role first, via check_admin_role passed $auth. Does not verify the role values inside the function; does not cover /api:app/admin/stats (wrong group).

Never touches tenants without filtering by org_id: every read/write of tenants must have an org_id predicate. Does not require the value to equal the caller's org (compare_to left empty deliberately).

ask_parts_not_covered.part: /admin as a URL path (endpoints under /admin, including api/app/admin/stats)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: no check selects by path; only api_groups, tags, tables, verbs and endpoint_auth exist. Used the admin API group as the closest match.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: 'before doing anything else' (strictly first, before any db read)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: partly covered: placement 'first' checks the role call is the first statement, but a literal reading also excludes any other preceding statement; the placement check is strict about the first statement only, and may not match db statements that do not read the caller

ask_parts_not_covered.part: filtering by org_id means the caller's own org
ask_parts_not_covered.why: needs runtime/org process: the ask does not say whether staff are org-scoped; I left it open and asked

assumptions: '/admin' means endpoints in the workspace's 'admin' API group (canonical 'admin', served at /api:admin).
'the tenants table' means table tenants, with field org_id (schema: int org_id to orgs).
The role-check function is check_admin_role (function/check_admin_role.xs), and its precondition enforces admin/support_lead.
Staff endpoints are cross-org, so org_id should be a filter presence check, not an equality with the caller's org.
Both policies advisory and active, per the skill's default for new policies.
workspace_names_used: table users, field role (admin, support_lead, member, viewer), org_id
endpoints api/admin/tenants_GET, api/admin/orgs/org_id/tenants_GET, api/admin/tenants/tenant_id_PATCH, api/admin/users_GET, api/app/admin/stats_GET
confusions: AUTH-002 template uses tags: ['admin'] to select endpoints and example function 'require_admin'; the workspace has no admin tag and the role function is named check_admin_role. The template says to 'fill' only the functions, so it's unclear whether tags should also be replaced by api_groups, which I did.

The check catalogue says api_groups selects endpoints only, but the parser warned that object.statement_required with api_groups inspects endpoints only and suggested object_kinds ['query']. The warning is correct but the skill doesn't say to set object_kinds alongside api_groups, so I found it only by parsing.
No path-based scope exists. 'Under /admin' has no direct check; the user's words map to a group or tag, and the skill's scoping section doesn't say what to do when the user names a URL path.
'placement first' can't express 'before any db read' vs 'first statement'. It is the first statement only; the skill doesn't explain how a preceding db.get is judged.

I was told not to run xano policy evaluate, so I can't confirm which findings the rules produce; my predicted findings are from reading the stacks and may be wrong, especially for db.where_constraint_required on db.get and count queries.

The partial-coverage note for 'before doing anything else' in ask_parts_not_covered is my own judgement, not something the skill states; the skill only defines placement 'first' as the first statement.
wished_for: A scope selector for URL path prefix (e.g. path_prefix: '/admin') or a way to tag API groups in one place.
A worked example of object.statement_required with api_groups + functions + placement first, to show it is endpoint-only and needs object_kinds.
A note on whether db.get/db.edit/count reads count for db.where_constraint_required (table_selector) and whether a predicate on the id field is enough.
Guidance on splitting one customer ask into several policies (one policy per file, but a mixed ask spanning two templates).
why_confidence: The role check and org_id filter are both expressible and parse cleanly, with one warning fixed. But: (a) the policy checks that check_admin_role is called first, not that it allows the right roles; (b) /admin is mapped to the admin API group, which misses api/app/admin/stats; (c) the org_id rule checks presence of a filter, not that it matches the caller's org; (d) I could not run xano policy evaluate, so the predicted findings are unverified.
